span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the quantity actually wanted - the rank - is replaced by the sum of the singular values, because minimising rank is NP-hard and every known exact algorithm takes time doubly exponential in the dimension, while the substitute is convex
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the substitution is licensed by an analogy the authors state rather than assume: the nuclear norm stands to the rank function as the convex l1 norm stands to the counting l0 norm in sparse signal recovery - one counts nonvanishing singular values, the other sums their amplitude
span.note: about this quote: Q-613, 2026-08-16: TWO FAILED GLYPHS INSIDE THIS QUOTE. The staged text reads "what the convex (cid:4)1 norm is to the counting (cid:4)0 norm" - the extraction could not map the script-l character and left the raw PDF font code "(cid:4)" in its place, twice. Read as l-1 and l-0, the standard sparse-recovery notation. The quote is an exact substring of the staged file. It is kept rather than dropped because this sentence IS the licence for the paper's central substitution - the nuclear norm stands to rank as the convex norm stands to the counting norm - and a mechanisms layer that silently omitted it would be tidier and less true.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the informal requirement that the singular vectors be spread out is converted into a MEASURED quantity - the coherence of a subspace against the standard basis - whose smallest value is one, attained when the spanning vectors' entries all share a magnitude, and whose largest is attained by any subspace containing a standard basis element
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: necessity is established by exhibiting a matrix rather than by argument: this one cannot be recovered from a sample of its entries unless nearly all are seen, because for most sampling sets one would see only zeros and would have no way to guess the matrix is not zero
span.note: about this quote: Q-613, 2026-08-16: THE SUBJECT OF THIS QUOTE IS ANAPHORIC AND ITS REFERENT IS NOT QUOTABLE. "this matrix" is the rank-one matrix with a single nonzero entry in the top-right corner, defined in the preceding sentence as M = e1 e_n^*. The span was NOT widened to reach that definition because the intervening text is the flattened matrix display, which the extraction renders as stray zeros and box-drawing characters - 'M = e1e* n = [ 0 0 ... 0 0 . . . 0 . . . ] , 0 1 0 0 ...' - so a wider span would quote rubble to fix a pronoun. Recorded here instead.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: a second necessary condition is derived the same way, from an adversarial sampling set rather than a random one: with no sample in some row, one component is unobserved and no method whatsoever can recover it, so at least one observation per row and per column is required
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the impossibility is side-stepped by changing the question from ALL sampling sets to MOST - adversarial sampling defeats even rank one, so what is asked instead is whether recovery succeeds for almost all sampling sets of a given size
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the class of matrices the theorem covers is fixed by an explicitly stated assumption rather than left to the reader: both coherences must be bounded above by a single positive constant, which is what turns 'the singular vectors are spread out' into a checkable premise
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the convex program is put into a form existing software already solves: for a positive semidefinite unknown the nuclear norm IS the trace of the matrix, so the heuristic collapses into minimising the trace over the constraint set
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The guarantee covers exactly low-rank matrices; extension to approximately low-rank matrices is left open.
span.note: what this limits: the exact-recovery guarantee: IT WOULD BE OF INTEREST TO EXTEND OUR RESULTS TO THE CASE WHERE THE UNKNOWN MATRIX IS APPROXIMATELY LOW-RANK - only exactly low-rank is covered
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The sampling bounds proved may be far more demanding than what is needed in practice.
span.note: what this limits: the sampling bound as a practical requirement: THE EXPERIMENTS REVEAL VERY SIMILAR PLOTS FOR DIFFERENT n, SUGGESTING THAT OUR ASYMPTOTIC CONDITIONS FOR RECOVERY MAY BE RATHER CONSERVATIVE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The semidefinite program the theory relies on does not scale with off-the-shelf solvers.
span.note: what this limits: any large-scale application of the method as specified: STANDARD INTERIOR POINT METHODS WILL BE IMPRACTICAL FOR PROBLEMS WHERE THE UNKNOWN MATRIX HAS HUNDREDS OF ROWS OR COLUMNS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The general problem of recovery from arbitrary linear functionals is not treated.
span.note: what this limits: the general recovery problem: WE LEAVE THIS GENERAL LOW-RANK RECOVERY PROBLEM FOR FUTURE WORK
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper states that the general problem is impossible and narrows the question before answering it.
span.note: what this limits: the exact-recovery result reported here: the authors state it is impossible to recover all low-rank matrices from sampled entries, and pose the answerable question as whether most can be recovered
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The tractable method is a relaxation whose equivalence to the real problem holds for most instances, not all.
span.note: what this limits: the use of nuclear norm minimisation as a stand-in for rank minimisation: the paper states the relaxation is formally equivalent to the combinatorially hard rank minimization problem for most problems
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The recovery guarantee holds only for matrices whose row and column spaces satisfy an incoherence condition.
span.note: what this limits: any application of this recovery result: it applies to matrices whose row and column spaces are incoherent with the standard basis, a property of the matrix that must hold for the guarantee to bind
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The exact-solution alternative is not merely slow but doubly exponential in the dimension.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that this method makes the problem tractable: the exact formulation is NP-hard and all known exact algorithms require time doubly exponential in the matrix dimension
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the compressed-sensing result that an object can be recovered exactly from far fewer measurements than its dimension, carried over from signal acquisition to the recovery of a low-rank matrix from a sample of its entries
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the whole recovery procedure repeated 50 times for every (n, m, r) triple
span.note: eliminates: a single lucky or unlucky draw of the sampled entries - 50 repetitions per parameter setting turn one outcome into a rate

span.label: 'exact' recovery - EXACT UNDER CONDITIONS, NOT IN GENERAL: recovery of the true matrix is proved for matrices incoherent with the standard basis and from a random sample, after the paper has stated that recovering ALL low-rank matrices is impossible, so the word describes the outcome when the hypotheses hold rather than the reach of the method
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the nuclear norm - A HEURISTIC STANDING IN FOR RANK: the problem actually wanted is combinatorially hard, the nuclear norm is introduced as a heuristic optimisation, and the theorem is that the two coincide for most problems - so the method solves a different problem that usually has the same answer
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: incoherence - THE HYPOTHESIS THE HEADLINE DEPENDS ON: the recoverable matrices are those whose row and column spaces are incoherent with the standard basis, a property nothing in an application guarantees and which the result cannot be quoted without
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
